core_claim: Industrial revolutions don't replace fuels — they stack them. Each revolution added a new primary-energy source on top of the previous ones, leaving us in 2026 burning more coal than ever, while the fourth revolution adds a new heavy electricity consumer — AI training compute — that is doubling its appetite every six months.
tension: The standard energy-transition story implies dirty-to-clean movement. The data shows dirty-to-dirtier-plus-some-clean: the world burns more coal in 2024 than in any prior year, the fossil share has dropped only 5 percentage points in 51 years, and AI training compute is becoming the newest 100+ MW load.
payoff: Stop calling the fourth industrial revolution the clean one. It's the one whose signature fuel is electricity-on-demand, scaling faster than any prior demand curve.
